lines.en: I tap on Touka’s name in my phone as the amount of interpersonal training I have forced myself to endure throughout my time here now somewhat allows me to remember plans I personally made.
And today is the day I planned on taking Touka out and “groveling” or whatever it is she’s going to get a high off of making me do.
To be honest, I can’t imagine there will be much groveling at all as, like me, I think she’s mostly just talk.
She’s far too kind to push me off the pedestal I’ve spent thirty-one (and more) years building and will probably just make me say generic nice things to her or something along those lines.
: Hello? Sensei?
Which means I have to hit her with my greatest pick-up line right now so I can sail smoothly through-out the rest of the day.
: Hey.
Or at least that’s what I would say if I knew any pick-up lines.
: Hay is for horses. And, as today will be your day of groveling, I demand a more formal greeting. One that is at least somewhat memorable.
: Welcome to today, esteemed and beautiful Touka Tsukioka. May fortune continue to favor you and may the gods smile down on your suspicious womanly figure.
: Suspicious?
: Yeah. It’s kind of unfair that you’re more physically developed than some women I know in their 30’s.
: Well, I shan’t say that was formal. But I suppose you’ve nailed the memorable bit.
: Yeah, I have a lot more experience than most when it comes to nailing things.
: Is that so? I didn’t take you as a handyman.
: I’m not a handyman, but I sure am handy with my hands.
: Well, yes. They are hands. They are handy by nature.
I hang up so I can completely restart this phone call in a way that is hopefully much less awkward.
: Hello again.
: I’m sorry you had to hear any of that.
: It’s fine. I was just about to do the same thing.
: This is why I don’t normally call people first-thing in the morning. Especially lately since it’s been getting way harder to pull myself out of dream-mentality.
: I suppose I can somewhat relate. To what do I owe the pleasure, though?
: I told you I was going to call today, didn’t I? We made plans to do stuff while I was out camping.
: I suppose we did. But I was under the impression that you were either going to cancel or just disappear again.
: Well, I guess this is me proving you wrong then. When can you meet up?
: Whenever I find out where we’ll be meeting up. Because, unlike you, I’ve already been awake for several hours- patiently waiting for your call.
: Bullshit. Just three seconds ago you said you expected me to cancel.
: Yes, that’s correct. I was just trying my hand at sarcasm, but I feel as if I haven’t quite gotten it down yet. If you want the truth, I just got out of the bath.
: I have no response to that that wouldn’t ruin this phone call.
: My! Look at you, Sensei — acting so uncharacteristically mature despite having just opened your eyes. I admire the restraint.
: It does make me feel slightly lonely, though
: Why would that make you-
: One hour. We can meet near the vending machine.
: Touka, we live in Japan. There’s a vending machine on every corner.
: You know the one I mean, Sensei.
: Ciao.
I’m annoyed because she’s right. There’s only one vending machine that holds any sort of significance for us, but even then it’s still just a machine.
Regardless — after getting dressed and preparing for the day, I walk out into the living room to find Ami watching television on the couch.
It’s a simple sight, but one that I’ve forgotten over the last several months. And I’m glad I can finally see it again, as silly as that sounds.
But when she asks me where I’m going, I lie.
There’s no need to. I’m sure she wouldn’t stop me if she knew the truth.

But I do it anyway, because there always needs to be something. And if there’s anything I’m good at (apart from nailing things or tormenting rich girls), it’s building mole hills for someone else to turn into mountains.
When I leave the house, I look behind me. But I’m not sure quite why.
I don’t think I’m being followed.
But I think I wish I was.
: Well, would you look at that? It’s only been forty-five minutes, Sensei. Were you so excited to see me that you left early?
: No, I just didn’t stop for coffee on the way over like I originally decided to.
: One sentence in and you’ve already ruined our date. Impressive.
: Sure. Except that this isn’t really a “date” and more of just a way for me to show you how sorry I am for causing you to worry for so long. I’m doing it for everyone.
: Wow, and now you’ve made it even worse. Is there no limit to your undesirableness?
: Not really, no. I just tend to say things like that when I’m worried about getting closer to someone.

: So you do see us getting closer...but you also see me the same way as everyone else...while setting up a meeting that only exists because I asked you to do something to prove that you don’t see me that way.
: I’m confused.
: So I’m just going to say it’s a date. And if that word does not accurately describe what’s truly happening here, you can internalize it, for doing the opposite will only make me feel unwanted.
: Sure. Do whatever you want. Just don’t expect me to take you to some fancy French restaurant like you did for me when you got to choose the date.
: Oh, I remember that day. It’s when you chose Chika over me. What a lovely memory.
: I barely knew you at the time, Touka.
: So you’re saying you’d choose differently if that contest took place today?
: Is everything you say today going to be carefully designed to make things as hard as possible?
: Am I making it hard now?
: That...
: I believe you interpreted that in a way you were not intended to.
: I’d believe you if you were wearing a different outfit.
: My...outfit has nothing to do with your perversion, Sensei! I should be free to wear what I want without your gaze lingering longer than it’s supposed to.
: How long is it supposed to? What’s the max amount of time?
: Somewhere between two and five seconds. Long enough to not draw attention to the fact that there is any lingering at all.
: I’m kind of surprised to hear that you have an actual number.
: Of course I have a number. It’d be irrational to expect everyone to completely ignore my assets. All I ask is that it be done in moderation and never mentioned verbally.
: Then I will keep it in mind. Literally.
: Well done, Sensei. Now, take me away from here before anyone realizes what we’re talking about.
: On it.
: Oh, and please inform me of what we’ll be doing as I’ve only brought approximately 500,000 yen with me and have decided it will be best to keep my spending to a minimum as it’s grovel-day.
: Yeah, I think that’ll be more than enough. And I’m not sure what we’re doing yet. But we’ll begin by going to your favorite place in the world.
: The Swiss Alps?!
: The subway.
: I hate you.
: Yeah, I know.
Touka and I arrive in the urban district after a brief subway ride and begin to wander around in search of something that looks interesting to both of us.
The thing is, there isn’t much at all that seems to interest both of us. The only thing I can think of that comes close is the movie theater, and all Touka wants to watch is horror.
: We’ve passed several museums, Sensei. Did you not think to take me into any of those?
: Museums don’t interest me.
: Yes, but you don’t matter today.
: Well, that was rather blunt.
: Only because it’s true. If you want me to believe I hold a special place in your heart, you must go out of your way to prove it to me.
: I see no purpose in allowing you to lean on me in your time of need if you will not offer the same to me when I require a shoulder.
: I didn’t realize right now was a time of need for you.
: I suppose it’s less a time of “need” and more a time of “want.” But what I want is not so easily put into words.
: I can’t imagine it would be if it requires my participation in any capacity. You’re sort of like ten leagues above me, Touka.
: Oh, it’s far more than that. But it doesn’t change the fact that I enjoy your company far more than someone like me ever should. But we all have our flaws, and mine appear to be that I like you.
: Not unconditionally, though.
: Would you prefer me as a mindless zombie who will love you no matter what?
: You’d be easier to hang out with, that’s for sure.
: I’m easy right now as well. You’re likely just over-thinking it. Or not thinking at all, but I’m going to give you the benefit of the doubt since you did show up today.
: Yeah. I kind of can’t afford to have you not liking me anymore. So if I need to put in some work to maintain our relationship every now and then, so be it.
: Oh, yay. I’ve always wanted to be someone’s chore.
: That’s not what I meant, Touka. If anything, I’m the chore here.
: You most certainly are. You’ve been a never-ending pain in my behind since the moment we first met.
: The first time we met was in Osako’s dojo. I didn’t become a pain until you were one of my students.
: I suppose you’re right.
: But it’s also because of you that I’m beginning to understand what “pain” is at all. And I can’t quite tell if I like it or not.
: What’s there to like about pain?
: The parts where it feels good.
: Your mind is wandering again, isn’t it?
: I’m beginning to believe it’s not “wandering” at all and that you’re just leading it into the darkest corners of Kumon-mi on purpose.
: On purpose? Now, why would I do that?
: Maybe you’re curious about what will happen there?
: Maybe I am? Then what?
: Is something wrong, Sensei? You’re walking a little...strangely all of a sudden.
: Just keep looking forward, Touka.

Eventually, our “date” leads us into a restaurant after we spend an hour or so wandering through a park — a park where Touka decided the best use of her money was lining the pockets of various street performers.
And yes, she’s generous. This is what she does. But there’s a point where generosity becomes dangerous. And she’s just lucky no one has attempted to take advantage of that yet.
I could if I wanted to. I know I could.
But there is something else I want from her instead.
Something that can’t be bought.
Or even understood by most — this endless Oedipal craving and the desire to both consume and be consumed by a single being that my existence could both start and end with.
So she looks at me, and I look back at her.
But while she sees a fancy jewel or an interesting mechanical toy, I see a blanket and a ball-gag. And I feel the sensation of someone sneaking into bed beside me.
: I heard you had a conversation with my mother recently.
: I’ve had many conversations with your mother. But I’m reluctant to divulge the details of any of them.
: And why is that?
: Two reasons. One — you don’t need to know. And two — you probably already do.
: I can see why you’d think that, but I assure you that my mother has no qualms at all with keeping information she does not wish to share away from me.
: So if you know I was there, it would have to mean she wants you to know I was there, right?
: Maybe.
: Or maybe I just have eyes.
: The kind you personally see with? Or the kind your sister has that are just stationed around Tsukioka Manor?
: I see you’ve learned of Tsukasa’s henchmen. Interesting. How did that come to be?
: Maybe I have eyes too?
: If you’ve been planting cameras around my home, I do hope you’ve omitted them from my bedrooms.
: I’ll have them removed next week. Scout’s honor.
: You saw us?
: Is that the conclusion you’ve drawn from that?
: It’s what you were implying, is it not?
: All I’m doing is offering up a potential explanation. I never said I actually saw anything.
: Regardless of what I know, though, I’d like to hear from you. What business do you have with my mother?
: I think a better question is what business Tsubasa has with me. I can never figure out what the hell she’s trying to do. Especially now that the whole Chika situation is under control.
: So she asked you for something?
: I didn’t say that.
: You didn’t answer the question either. She did, didn’t she?
: Why not just ask her?
: Why not just tell me?
: Because I have no idea what she’s okay with me sharing and acknowledge the fact that she could put me in prison whenever she wants.
: True. But then she’d need to find someone else to pique her interest, and that doesn’t happen very often. And besides, I could put you in prison if I wanted to as well.
: Sure. But then you’d need to find someone else to pique your interest, and I don’t think that happens very often.
: And you’d be right in thinking that. But there’s something I’d like to ask you, Sensei. Or rather...something I’d appreciate your participation in.
: Oh good. Here we go again. Your family really has it out for me, don’t they?
: Sensei...all I want is for you to stop giving her the time of day.
: What?

: She’s gotten too interested in...interfering. And I’d very much like her to mind her own business when it comes to my personal affairs. But, so long as you keep letting her tug your strings, she has no reason to stop.
: Is just knowing you don’t want her getting involved not enough?
: Not when she knows I can’t and won’t do anything about it.
: But why not? You’re the...future heir or whatever, aren’t you? Can’t you leverage that to get her to back off?
: Hah...no. That’s my duty, and it’s separate from my personal life. If I begin conflating the two, it’ll blur the lines my ancestors have so meticulously drawn.
: These two things must remain separate no matter what. Which means that the only thing I can leverage is the fact that I’m my mother’s daughter and that I’d like some privacy.
: But we Tsukiokas aren’t typically great when it comes to “privacy.” And that’s especially true for my mother who suddenly wants to know every explicit detail of my personal life.
: But the strangest part is that she rarely expressed any interest in that until I began spending time with you.
: Well...why do you think that is?
: I have my guesses. But I don’t think I can share any of them inside of a restaurant.
: If that is what this place is, I mean. Because I’m not quite sure I’ve ever seen food that looks like this before.
: That is fried chicken, Touka.
: Then why is it so shiny and round?
: Asset limitations. Just ignore it and look at me.
: Apologies.
: Talk to her if you don’t want her interfering. Don’t put that on me.
: Do you think I haven’t tried that? It’s as if she refuses to let me have anything without also sharing it with her.
: It’s quite infuriating, to be honest. But there’s only so much I can do.
: You can do way more than I can, Touka.
: Because even though Tsubasa hasn’t really done anything bad to me yet, she knows enough about me that she definitely could.
: But I don’t know enough about her yet to know if she actually would. You know?
: I suppose I understand what you’re saying. I just didn’t take you as the type to let someone like that boss you around.
: Then you don’t know me very well yet, I guess.
: Oh well. I suppose this just means that I get to boss you around too now that I know things about you.
: In a roundabout way, that’s almost what this date is.
: In a roundabout way, I think I’d have to agree.
: But that calls into question just what else I can get you to do for me...
Touka’s affection has increased to [touka_love]!
